task: what happened to hub w2 compared with last week?
answer:
Hub W2 is currently operating at 157% of its daily capacity, with 25 parcels on-site for 21 customers and 12 parcels currently late.

*   Hub W2 has a rated capacity of 14 parcels per day, but is currently handling a load ratio of 1.57.
*   The on-time delivery rate for this week is 77%, failing the 90% commitment in the "Courier Y agreement (service terms)" and the 85% requirement for the "Offer 2-day delivery to west customers" decision.
*   "Run the Festive Flash Sale (40% off kitchen) in the west" and "Run the Winter Sale (25% off home) in the west" both assumed hub capacity would remain within limits, but the load ratio is now 1.57.
*   The "Winter Sale" starts in 10 days, and its parcels are routed through Hub W2; a reroute to Hub W4 is available, which would take 14 hours and has a capacity of 10.
*   There are 21 customers waiting for 25 parcels with a total order value of $1,929.89; 7 are gold-tier customers and 9 parcels are past their delivery date.
*   The largest waiting orders are $212.51 (gold), $201.35 (gold, 24 hours late), and $181.89 (standard, 36 hours late).
*   "Switch west region deliveries to Courier Y to cut cost" is relied upon by "End the west backup courier contract" and "Offer 2-day delivery to west customers".
*   At the same time, the FEST40 campaign ran during the window; 58% of parcels through Hub W2 in the window used its coupon. This is an overlap in the data, not proof of cause.
*   "Operations meeting notes, 18 Aug" noted that backup couriers previously covered peaks, but "Operations meeting notes, 17 Sep" recorded the decision to end that contract based on the assumption that Hub W2 could carry volume alone.

draft:
Hub W2: 25 parcels there now for 21 customers, 12 late; on time this week 77%; capacity 14 a day.
Winter Sale plan, "Delivery check": Assumption: Hub W2 can carry the Winter Sale volume. To be confirmed with logistics a week before launch.
Courier Y agreement (service terms), "Service level": Courier Y runs all west deliveries through Hub W2 and commits to at least 90% of parcels on time each week. Hub W2 is rated for 14 parcels a day.
Operations meeting notes, 18 Aug, "Risk raised": Support asked what happens in sale weeks, because Hub W2 handles only 14 parcels a day. Answer: the backup courier covers peaks for now. Follow-up: review the backup contract in September.
"Switch west region deliveries to Courier Y to cut cost" assumed courier Y delivers at least 90% on time through Hub W2; it is now 77% (needed 90%).
At the same time, the FEST40 campaign ran during the window; 58% of parcels through Hub W2 in the window used its coupon. That is an overlap in the data, not proof of cause.
"Offer 2-day delivery to west customers" assumed west deliveries via W2 are 85% on time; it is now 77% (needed 85%).
"Run the Festive Flash Sale (40% off kitchen) in the west" assumed hubs can handle the sale volume within daily capacity; it is now 1.57x capacity (needed 1.00x).
Winter Sale starts in 10 days and its parcels go through Hub W2, which is already struggling.
21 customers are still waiting on 25 parcels at Hub W2 ($1,929.89 of orders; 7 gold; 9 already past their delivery date). Largest waiting orders: $212.51 (gold), $201.35 (gold, 24 h late), $181.89 (standard, 36 h late); 2 other decisions rely on this one: "End the west backup courier contract"; "Offer 2-day delivery to west customers".
